criteria_evidence.C1: Five investor-specific prompts cover competence, balance-sheet quality, growth and price. Each is roughly 2–3 KB and requests only 2–4 thesis sentences; no primary-source distilled corpus is provided.

criteria_evidence.C3: Graham uses earning power and book value; Lynch uses PEG and categories; Munger uses inversion; Druckenmiller uses fundamental inflections. These qualitative checklists share the same input snapshot.
criteria_evidence.C4: Hard point-in-time input rule, neutral/abstention for insufficient history, schema validation, persisted prompts and responses, and documented approximation/impersonation limits. Missing individual numerical fields are not systematically prevented.

Druckenmiller intentionally lacks macro, rates, price-action inputs.
MIN_PERIODS counts metric rows, not semantic field coverage; stock-specific important fields may still be absent.
